about: Fragment selection for the ci workflow. Unlike the others it has no single loading section: step-02 loads the Pact set when contract testing is in play, step-03 loads the burn-in set and the Pact gate set. Both step files are supplied as ground truth. The ci_platform axis is deliberately exercised, because a pipeline generator is the workflow most likely to be written and tested against GitHub Actions alone.

cases.name: GitLab CI for a Python service
cases.prompt: Generate our GitLab CI pipeline for the invoices service, with quality gates on the test suite.
repoFacts: .gitlab-ci.yml already exists and is the project's pipeline; there is no .github/ directory
pyproject.toml with pytest; there is no package.json in the repo
no pact artifacts, no browser automation, no .maestro directory

assertions.text: ci-burn-in.md is the burn-in guidance for every platform. GitLab rather than GitHub Actions changes the template that gets written, not which knowledge the run needs, and treating the two as linked is how a workflow ends up implicitly GitHub-only.

burn-in.md and playwright-utils-mandate.md load only when the flag is on AND the stack is Playwright. A Python repo with no package.json satisfies neither half, so the utility-driven selection path stays closed and ci-burn-in.md is the whole answer.

cases.name: Pipeline for a consumer with contract tests
cases.prompt: Generate the CI pipeline and the quality gates for the billing web client, including publishing pacts and gating deploys on can-i-deploy.
repoFacts: tests/contract/ contains .pacttest.ts files and vitest.config.pact.ts exists
PACT_BROKER_BASE_URL is set in the environment

assertions.text: pactjs-utils-provider-verifier.md is required even on a consumer-only pipeline, because the vitest pool and singleFork rule it carries applies to consumer and provider alike. Skipping it as provider-side reading is the plausible wrong call.
pact-broker-webhooks.md is loaded because a webhook failure silently breaks can-i-deploy, which is the gate this pipeline is being asked to build.
